units.text: Debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy when an assertion fails. Compose provides a native failure handling pipeline to streamline diagnostics. You can automatically capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon failure, or register custom handlers to forward crash telemetry to external tools.

quotes.quote: Debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy when an assertion fails.

Compose provides a native failure handling pipeline to streamline diagnostics. You can automatically capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon failure, or register custom handlers to forward crash telemetry to external tools.

units.text: The APIs associated with the failure handler pipeline (`TestFailurePolicy`, `TestFailureHandler`, and `FailureContext`) are included in `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.13.0-alpha01+` and `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:1.13.0-alpha01+`.

quotes.quote: The APIs associated with the failure handler pipeline (TestFailurePolicy, TestFailureHandler, and FailureContext) are included in androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.13.0-alpha01+ and androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:1.13.0-alpha01+.

units.text: To configure failure handling, pass a `TestFailurePolicy` object to `ComposeUiTestConfig`. To capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon test failure, set the `screenshotCaptureMode` and `uiHierarchyCaptureMode` properties in `TestFailurePolicy`.

quotes.quote: To configure failure handling, pass a
To capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon test failure, set the
properties in TestFailurePolicy.

class MyComposeTest { private val customConfig = ComposeUiTestConfig( failurePolicy = TestFailurePolicy( screenshotCaptureMode = TestFailurePolicy.CaptureMode.Enabled, uiHierarchyCaptureMode = TestFailurePolicy.CaptureMode.Enabled ) ) @Test fun myFirstTest() = runComposeUiTest(config = customConfig) {

units.text: To define custom behavior for test failures, add a `TestFailureHandler` to the `failureHandlers` list. Each handler receives a `FailureContext` object that contains the original error and a list of artifacts generated by the preceding pipeline handlers.

quotes.quote: To define custom behavior for test failures, add a
Each handler receives a FailureContext object that contains the original error and a list of artifacts generated by the preceding pipeline handlers.

class MyComposeTestWithHandler { private val customConfig = ComposeUiTestConfig( failurePolicy = TestFailurePolicy( screenshotCaptureMode = TestFailurePolicy.CaptureMode.Enabled, failureHandlers = listOf( TestFailureHandler { context -> val screenshot = context.artifacts.firstOrNull { it.type == FailureArtifact.Type.Screenshot } // ... } ) ) ) @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule(config = customConfig)

units.text: You can enable failure artifact captures for an entire test suite by passing instrumentation runner arguments in your module's `build.gradle` file. This eliminates the need to update individual test files.

units.text: The framework evaluates both the local `TestFailurePolicy` and the suite-level runner arguments:

quotes.quote: The framework evaluates both the local TestFailurePolicy and the suite-level runner arguments:

units.text: Starting with Robolectric 4.15, it's possible to launch an interactive preview of your app or tests in a Robolectric environment. The Robolectric simulator can be a useful way to preview how your UI would look in a Robolectric environment. This can be helpful, for instance, when debugging failing Robolectric tests.

quotes.quote: Starting with Robolectric 4.15, it's possible to launch an interactive preview of your app or tests in a Robolectric environment.
The Robolectric simulator can be a useful way to preview how your UI would look in a Robolectric environment. This can be helpful, for instance, when debugging failing Robolectric tests.

units.text: The Robolectric simulator is highly experimental and is still largely in the proof-of-concept stage. UI rendered in the Robolectric simulator may not match an Android emulator or device 100%.

quotes.quote: Note that the Robolectric simulator is highly experimental and is still largely in the proof-of-concept stage.
UI rendered in the Robolectric simulator may not match an Android emulator or device 100%.

units.text: There are two ways to launch the simulator: with the simulator Gradle plugin or by invoking the simulator APIs from tests. To enable the Robolectric simulator with the Gradle plugin, add the plugin to the plugins block of your app's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` file:

quotes.quote: There are two ways to launch the simulator: with the simulator Gradle plugin or by invoking the simulator APIs from tests.
To enable the Robolectric simulator with the Gradle plugin, add the plugin to the plugins block of your app's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file:

units.text: id("org.robolectric.simulator") version "1.0.3"

quotes.quote: id("org.robolectric.simulator") version "1.0.3"

units.text: Then, run `./gradlew simulate<variant>` (for example, `./gradlew simulateDebug` or `./gradlew simulateDemoDebug`) to start the simulator for the `<variant>` build variant. It will run the main Activity that is configured in your manifest.

quotes.quote: Then, run ./gradlew simulate<variant> (for example, ./gradlew simulateDebug or ./gradlew simulateDemoDebug) to start the simulator for the <variant> build variant. It will run the main Activity that is configured in your manifest.

units.text: To enable the simulator to work with JDK 23 and newer, you must add the following extra jvmArgs to your unit test configuration:

quotes.quote: To enable the simulator to work with JDK 23 and newer, you must add the following extra jvmArgs to your unit test configuration:

testOptions { unitTests { all { test -> test.jvmArgs( "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.awt=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.base/sun.reflect.misc=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.base/sun.security.action=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.swing=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.lwawt.macosx=ALL-UNNAMED", ) } } }

units.text: Inside a Robolectric test, you can also start the simulator using the standalone API. To do this, first add a dependency to the simulator in your project's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` file.

quotes.quote: Inside a Robolectric test, you can also start the simulator using the standalone API. To do this, first add a dependency to the simulator in your project's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file.

units.text: Next, you can create a `Simulator` object and start it using:

quotes.quote: Next, you can create a Simulator object and start it using:

import android.os.Build.VERSION_CODES.VANILLA_ICE_CREAM import org.junit.Test import org.junit.runner.RunWith import org.robolectric.Robolectric import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner import org.robolectric.annotation.Config import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode import org.robolectric.simulator.Simulator @RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class) @Config(sdk = [VANILLA_ICE_CREAM]) @GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE) class MainActivityTest { @Test fun simulateMainActivity() { Robolectric.setupActivity(MainActivity::class.java) Simulator().start() } }

units.text: The 2019 Robolectric blog post on PAUSED LooperMode says that in PAUSED mode, Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue. This is a hint that the unexecuted behavior is important for the test case.

quotes.quote: Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue. This is a hint that the unexecuted behavior is important for the test case.

units.text: The same post says AndroidX Test APIs, like `ActivityScenario`, `FragmentScenario` and Espresso will automatically idle the main Looper.

quotes.quote: AndroidX Test APIs, like ActivityScenario, FragmentScenario and Espresso will automatically idle the main Looper.

units.text: The post's troubleshooting section says: if you see test failures like `Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables`, you may need to insert `shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()` calls to your test to drain the main Looper. It's recommended to step through your test code with a watch set on `Looper.getMainLooper().getQueue()` to see the status of the Looper queue, to determine the appropriate point to add a `shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()` call.

units.text: - If your tests fail after upgrading to v2, they likely exhibit the following pattern: you launch a task (for example, a ViewModel loads data), but your assertion fails immediately because the data is still in a "Loading" state. With the v2 APIs, coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately. Explicitly advance time: use `waitForIdle` or `runOnIdle` to execute queued tasks before asserting.

Fix: Explicitly advance time.

// Explicitly run all queued tasks

units.text: - When migrating complex UIs to Compose, you might encounter identical Compose elements nested inside multiple traditional Android Views, such as within a `RecyclerView` or a `ViewPager`. In these scenarios, a standard Compose search like `onNodeWithText("Save")` might fail with a "Multiple nodes found" error. Use the `onRootWithViewInteraction` API on your test rule. This function accepts an Espresso `ViewInteraction`. The `onRootWithViewInteraction` API is included in `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4:1.12.0-alpha01+` and `androidx.compose.ui:ui-test:1.12.0-alpha01+`. This API is experimental and subject to change.

units.text: - **Timezone handling.** When using `SimpleDateFormat#parse()` to parse a timezone using the `Z` marker, Android supports time zones with a colon (i.e. 08:00), while OpenJDK doesn't (i.e. 0800). To work around this, if your min SDK version is 24 or higher, you can use the `X` marker instead; use the `java.time` API, with library desugaring enabled; or run the corresponding tests using regular Android tests.

units.text: - **Month names.** When using `DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(String)` to create a formatter displaying a short month name (using the `MMM` pattern), Android will use three-characters names (i.e. Jan), while OpenJDK will use three-characters names followed by a period (i.e. Jan.). In this case, Robolectric recommends running the corresponding tests as regular Android tests.
